curriculum.lesson_evidence: When you perform your dance, start in a still shape, focus your eyes, move with confidence and hold the final shape. If you make a mistake, keep going. Afterwards, the audience gives feedback as two stars and a wish, using dance words such as level, speed, energy and formation. Describe what you saw first and then say how it made you feel with a reason. The performer listens, says thank you and writes one change for the next time.

Afterwards, the audience gives feedback as two stars and a wish, using dance words such as level, speed, energy and formation. lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Give feedback on a dance you saw using one star and one wish. Use a dance word in each.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: 'Star: the quick steps made the storm feel exciting. Wish: hold the last shape longer.' Each comment names a dance element and says what it did for the audience.

WATCH FOR
Thinking that feedback is about saying who is the best dancer. Feedback is about the dance elements and helps the dancer improve, not about ranking people.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Perform your story dance for family. Ask them for a star and a wish using dance words. Write down their comments and one change you will make, then perform it again with the change.

Write a short reflection naming one artistic choice you changed and why. Movement or instrument work is optional, adult-supervised and can be described instead.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Example: After Pia's performance, a classmate says, 'Star: your slow turns and low levels looked like melting snow. Star: your final shape was very still. Wish: use bigger arms in the middle.' Pia says, 'Thank you,' and writes: 'Next time: bigger arms.' She keeps going when she wobbled at the start.

TRY FIRST
Give feedback on a dance you saw using one star and one wish. Use a dance word in each.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: 'Star: the quick steps made the storm feel exciting. Wish: hold the last shape longer.' Each comment names a dance element and says what it did for the audience.
teach_steps.explain:
When you perform your dance, start in a still shape, focus your eyes, move with confidence and hold the final shape. If you make a mistake, keep going. Afterwards, the audience gives feedback as two stars and a wish, using dance words such as level, speed, energy and formation. Describe what you saw first and then say how it made you feel with a reason. The performer listens, says thank you and writes one change for the next time.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make intentional visual, music, drama or dance choices and name their effect, rather than saying an artwork is simply “nice”. Keep every claim linked to an element or technique.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the elements, techniques or performance choices that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. For movement or instruments, use a clear space, ask an adult to be nearby and stop if anything feels unsafe. You may always describe a choice instead of performing it. One deliberate artistic choice with a named effect is more useful than a longer praise sentence.
